title: Implement Stipend Hold Policy for Overdue Accounts
description: EduPay Ledger Academy, a sophisticated fintech platform for educational institutions, needs to implement a new risk-mitigation policy. The current system disburses financial aid stipends via a saga pattern orchestrated by the `financial_aid_service`. However, there is no check to prevent disbursing funds to students with delinquent accounts. The new policy requires that before a stipend is disbursed, the system must verify the student's account status with the `bursar_service`. If the account has an overdue balance, the stipend disbursement must be placed on hold, a `StipendHeld` event must be published for administrative review, and the saga must terminate gracefully. This task requires a deep understanding of the existing microservice, CQRS, and Saga patterns to implement a robust, cross-service solution.

project_spec.name: EduPay Ledger Academy
project_spec.description:
EduPay Ledger Academy is an expert-level fintech payment platform designed specifically for higher-education institutions and EdTech providers. It enables campuses, online course marketplaces, and scholarship funds to orchestrate complex tuition, stipend, and micro-credential transactions while teaching computer-science students how production-grade payment rails are engineered. Built in C and structured with Robert C. Martin’s Clean Architecture, each business rule stands isolated from frameworks so that professors can swap out databases, message brokers, or UI shells during coursework without touching the core domain. 

The system embeds curated lessons within its codebase: every bounded context (Admissions, Bursar, Financial-Aid, Continuing-Education) contains annotated examples of payment_processing, multi_currency settlement, fraud_detection heuristics, and regulatory_compliance flows (FERPA-aware KYC, PCI-DSS, PSD2). Instructors can activate the Saga Pattern demonstration mode, where simulated outages force learners to debug distributed rollbacks across microservices. Event Sourcing and CQRS projections power real-time dashboards used by students in risk_assessment labs, while an immutable Audit_Trail doubles as a data set for coursework on compliance_reporting and encryption strategies. By combining hands-on financial operations with pedagogical scaffolding, EduPay Ledger Academy transforms a mission-critical fintech backend into a living textbook.
dependencies: libevent or libuv – high-performance event loop for microservice runtimes
grpc-c / protobuf-c – service-to-service RPC with contract-first schema
confluent-kafka-c – Kafka client for Event Sourcing and CQRS projections
libpq (PostgreSQL) + TimescaleDB extension – relational store for read models and risk analytics
SQLite (optional, in-memory) – lightweight option for classroom demos
OpenSSL / libsodium – TLS and envelope encryption for Security_by_Design
jansson – JSON parsing/serialization for API adapters
libcurl – outbound HTTP/REST integrations (e.g., bank APIs, KYC vendors)
nats.c – lightweight message bus for Saga orchestrations
uthash / klib – utility data structures for domain entities in pure C
cmocka – unit testing harness aligned with clean architecture boundaries
docker compose / Buildah scripts – containerized deployment for microservices clusters
